text_en: According to the 2025 European Commission Report, the Republic of Moldova has some level of preparation in the area of freedom of movement for workers.
summary: The PNA reports the Commission's 2025 rating: Moldova has some level of preparation on freedom of movement for workers.
extraction_note: The Government restates the Commission's standard wording ("some level of preparation"); eu_scale is left empty because the item is not from an EU source. The duplicated "de de" is as printed.

text_en: Considerable progress was made in signing bilateral agreements on the coordination of social security systems with EU Member States and in continuing preparatory work to join the European network of employment services (EURES) upon EU accession.
summary: Reported Commission view: considerable progress on bilateral social security agreements with Member States and on preparations to join EURES upon accession.
extraction_note: Part of the Government's summary of the Commission's 2025 report.

text_en: The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection is the authority responsible for coordinating the working group for Chapter 2 "Freedom of movement for workers".
summary: The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection coordinates the Chapter 2 accession working group.
extraction_note: Designation of an institution (M2), recorded as adopted because it is stated as current.
intervention_as_stated: Designation of MMPS as coordinator of the Chapter 2 working group

text_en: The legislation in force on labour migration treats citizens of the European Union as "foreign citizens", applying to them the same rules as to other categories of foreigners on the territory of the Republic of Moldova.
summary: Current labour-migration law treats EU citizens as foreigners, under the same rules as other foreigners in Moldova.

text_en: However, foreigners holding a temporary right of residence for work or study do not benefit from this access.
summary: Foreigners with temporary residence for work or study have no access to employment services and active labour market measures.
extraction_note: "This access" refers to the preceding sentence: the full package of employment services and active measures available to foreigners, including EU citizens, with temporary or permanent residence, statelessness or international protection. Same rule restated at page 428 under Law 105/2018; not extracted again (M3).

text_en: Currently, the provisions of Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners in the Republic of Moldova apply to EU citizens. Foreign citizens, including EU citizens, must obtain a temporary residence permit for work on the territory of the Republic of Moldova in order to be employed.
summary: Under Law 200/2010, EU citizens, like other foreigners, currently need a temporary residence permit for work to be employed in Moldova.
extraction_note: Describes the current legal situation under a named law; recorded as a finding because the claim is the work-permit requirement, not the law as a measure. Could also be read as an intervention (Law 200/2010, adopted).

text_en: The above-mentioned law expressly provides that the temporary right of residence for work is granted for a period of up to one year, with the possibility of extension for a new term.
summary: Under Law 200/2010 the temporary right of residence for work is granted for up to one year and can be extended.
extraction_note: The next sentence (pages 426-427) gives up to two years for foreigners on investment projects of national importance or in priority occupations; not extracted separately.

text_en: In 2023, amendments were made to Law No. 200/2010, under which citizens of EU Member States have the right, for 90 days in any period of 180 calendar days of stay on the territory of the Republic of Moldova, to work without obtaining a residence permit for work (without any formalities).
summary: 2023 amendments to Law 200/2010 let EU citizens work in Moldova without a work residence permit for 90 days in any 180.
intervention_as_stated: Amendments to Law No. 200/2010 on the regime of foreigners (2023)

text_en: Law No. 200/2025 on the free movement and residence on the territory of the Republic of Moldova of citizens of the European Union and their family members, recently adopted, introduces a clear legal distinction between EU citizens and third-country nationals. This law significantly simplifies the documentation procedures applicable to EU citizens residing in the Republic of Moldova.
summary: The recently adopted Law 200/2025 distinguishes EU citizens from third-country nationals and simplifies documentation procedures for EU citizens residing in Moldova.
extraction_note: The text then says that on its entry into force Law 200/2010 will no longer apply to EU citizens and their family members, so the law is adopted but not yet in force at the time of writing.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025 privind libera circulație și șederea pe teritoriul Republicii Moldova a cetățenilor Uniunii Europene și a membrilor familiilor acestora

text_en: EU citizens will not be required to obtain a work authorisation or a residence permit for employment. For stays of up to 90 days, they may carry out lawful activities on the territory of the Republic of Moldova without additional formalities.
summary: Under Law 200/2025, EU citizens will need no work authorisation or employment residence permit; stays up to 90 days need no formalities.
extraction_note: Future effect of Law 200/2025 ("odată cu intrarea în vigoare"); status follows the law, which is adopted.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025 (provisions applying on entry into force)

text_en: For a stay exceeding 90 days, EU citizens will have to obtain a residence card, issued by the General Inspectorate for Migration (IGM), which is not conditional on a particular purpose of stay. The residence card is granted for up to 5 years and gives the holder the right to carry out any lawful activity, while guaranteeing the rights and obligations provided by national law.
summary: Under Law 200/2025, EU citizens staying over 90 days need an IGM residence card, valid up to five years, allowing any lawful activity.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025 (residence card for EU citizens)

text_en: The law (Law No. 105/2018) provides that foreign citizens with a temporary or permanent right of residence, recognised stateless persons and beneficiaries of international protection or political asylum (except foreigners with temporary residence for work or study) are subject to the same rules as Moldovan citizens in accessing, where needed, employment services and active measures.
summary: Law 105/2018 gives resident foreigners the same access to employment services as nationals, except holders of residence for work or study.
extraction_note: The preceding sentence (pages 427-428) says Law 105/2018 guarantees equal access of nationals and foreign citizens to employment promotion services and measures, listed among acts applied to avoid discrimination of EU citizens. Quote limited to page 428 because the quote check drops one-word lines at page boundaries in this file as running headers. The exclusion is also stated at page 426 (finding).
intervention_as_stated: Legea Nr. 105/2018 cu privire la promovarea ocupării forței de muncă și asigurarea de șomaj

text_en: EU citizens benefit from free access to all jobs in the Republic of Moldova, except public functions that expressly require Moldovan citizenship.
summary: EU citizens have free access to all jobs in Moldova except public functions expressly requiring Moldovan citizenship.
extraction_note: Sits next to the statement (page 426) that EU citizens currently need a work residence permit; the two are recorded as stated, not reconciled.

text_en: Under recent amendments made by Government Decision No. 566/2025 to Annex 5 to Government Decision No. 201/2009 on the application of the Law on the public function, posts in the categories "technical service post", "specialist post" and "auxiliary post" may be filled by persons without Moldovan citizenship or stateless persons, employed under an individual employment contract under the Labour Code.
summary: Government Decision 566/2025 opens technical, specialist and auxiliary posts in the public service to non-citizens and stateless persons on employment contracts.
extraction_note: Quotation marks are mixed as printed.
intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 566/2025

text_en: Following a detailed analysis of the legal acts on public service management, a decision will be taken on the category of functions or posts that may be opened to EU citizens.
summary: After analysing public service legislation, the Government will decide which public functions or posts can be opened to EU citizens.
extraction_note: See also Annex B action 21 (analytical note on EU citizens' access to public functions, August 2026).
intervention_as_stated: Analysis of public service legislation to decide which posts open to EU citizens

text_en: Within the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, about 35 persons are involved in transposing EU acts on access to the labour market, employment support, equality and social advantages.
summary: About 35 Ministry of Labour staff work on transposing EU acts on labour-market access, employment support, equality and social advantages.

text_en: The National Employment Agency (ANOFM) will play a central role in ensuring access of Member State citizens to employment services and active labour market measures.
summary: ANOFM is to play the central role in giving Member State citizens access to employment services and active measures.
extraction_note: Assignment of a role to an institution (M2), stated in the future tense.
intervention_as_stated: Role of ANOFM in EU citizens' access to employment services

text_en: In this context, the 35 territorial employment subdivisions will be involved, with a staff ceiling of 189 persons (including 9 posts under moratorium), of which 176 posts are filled.
summary: ANOFM's 35 territorial subdivisions, to be involved, have a ceiling of 189 posts, 176 filled.

text_en: At central level, the National Employment Agency has a staff ceiling of 56 persons (including 2 posts under moratorium), of which 45 are filled.
summary: ANOFM's central office has a ceiling of 56 posts, 45 filled.

text_en: Labour Migration and EURES Directorate (staff ceiling 6 posts, of which 5 are filled);
summary: ANOFM's Labour Migration and EURES Directorate has 6 posts, 5 filled.
extraction_note: One of nine ANOFM central subdivisions listed (pages 428-429); only this one is specific to Chapter 2. The others (including the IT Directorate, 5 of 5) are not extracted.

text_en: The National Social Insurance House employs 1084 specialists, of whom 732 in the territory and 352 in the central office.
summary: CNAS employs 1084 specialists, 732 in the territory and 352 in the central office.
extraction_note: Staffing of the CNAS directorates (pages 429 and 439) not extracted separately except the international relations directorate (page 439).

text_en: The State Labour Inspectorate (ISM) and its territorial subdivisions carried out 2599 inspections in 2024 on compliance with labour legislation, of which 1267 on employment relations, 46 on occupational safety and health, 1269 combined, and 17 on labour migration.
summary: In 2024 the State Labour Inspectorate carried out 2599 inspections, 17 of them on labour migration.
extraction_note: In scope for the 17 labour-migration inspections (foreign workers); the other figures (pages 429-430: employees covered, wage arrears recovered, staff 83 planned and 65 employed) are general labour inspection and not extracted.

text_en: Under Article 5(8) of Law No. 200/2025, the Equality Council is given the competence to promote, monitor and support the application of the principle of equal treatment for EU citizens and their family members in exercising the right to free movement.
summary: Law 200/2025 designates the Equality Council to promote, monitor and support equal treatment of EU citizens and family members exercising free movement.
extraction_note: Designation of an institution by law (M2). Restated at page 432 (2.2) together with the planned staff increase, extracted there separately.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025, art. 5(8): Equality Council as equal treatment body

text_en: The Equality Council will also act as national contact point for preventing and combating discrimination, responsible for cooperation with similar authorities in EU Member States and Schengen states, ensuring exchange of data and information with them for implementing this law.
summary: The Equality Council will be the national contact point cooperating and exchanging information with equality bodies of EU and Schengen states.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025: Equality Council as national contact point

text_en: The Equality Council has 33 planned staff, of whom 19 are employed.
summary: The Equality Council has 33 planned posts and 19 staff.

text_en: The Anti-discrimination Directorate (ceiling 7 posts, 4 filled), which assists Council members in examining and resolving complaints of alleged discrimination.
summary: The Equality Council's anti-discrimination directorate, which handles complaints, has 7 posts, 4 filled.
extraction_note: The communication directorate (5 posts, 2 filled) is not extracted.

text_en: To ensure respect for the right to free movement, the Ministry of Internal Affairs is responsible for aligning policies on managing migration processes with European legislation.
summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs is responsible for aligning migration management policies with EU law to ensure free movement.
extraction_note: What an institution does (M2). The MAI policy directorate has 8 staff (same page), not extracted.

text_en: Thus the Ministry of Internal Affairs together with the General Inspectorate for Migration are responsible for transposing Directive 2004/38/EC on the right of EU citizens and their family members to move and reside freely.
summary: The Ministry of Internal Affairs and the General Inspectorate for Migration are responsible for transposing Directive 2004/38/EC.

text_en: In this context, in 2024 a cooperation agreement was signed between the General Inspectorate for Migration and the State Labour Inspectorate, regulating direct cooperation at central and territorial level on preventing and combating labour illegalities and on the regime of foreigners in Moldova.
summary: In 2024 the Migration Inspectorate and the Labour Inspectorate signed a cooperation agreement on labour illegalities and the regime of foreigners.
extraction_note: Enforcement against illegal employment of foreigners; kept as it concerns foreign workers in Moldova. IGM investigation staff (4 central, 18 regional, page 431) not extracted.
intervention_as_stated: Acordul de colaborare IGM–ISM (2024)

text_en: Law No. 200/2025 partially transposed Regulation (EU) No 492/2011 on freedom of movement for workers and Directive 77/486/EEC on the education of children of migrant workers, and fully transposed Directive 2014/54/EU on measures facilitating the exercise of workers' free movement rights.
summary: Law 200/2025 partially transposed Regulation 492/2011 and Directive 77/486/EEC and fully transposed Directive 2014/54/EU.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr. 200/2025

text_en: The Ministry of Education and Research, the Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development, the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection and the Equality Council are in the process of adjusting secondary legislation in their areas of competence.
summary: Four institutions are adjusting secondary legislation in their areas to implement Law 200/2025.
intervention_as_stated: Adjustment of secondary legislation following Law 200/2025

text_en: The Ministry of Labour and Social Protection is amending Government Decision No. 1276/2018 on procedures for access to employment measures to give EU citizens access to the services and active measures offered by ANOFM.
summary: The Ministry of Labour is amending Government Decision 1276/2018 to give EU citizens access to ANOFM services and active measures.
extraction_note: Also Annex A normative action 1 (deadline April 2026), extracted separately because the annex adds the deadline and responsible bodies.
intervention_as_stated: Amendment of Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 1276/2018

text_en: ANOFM staff will be trained on how to deal with EU citizens and their family members when providing employment support measures.
summary: ANOFM staff will be trained on serving EU citizens and family members when providing employment support.
extraction_note: Also Annex B action 1.
intervention_as_stated: Training of ANOFM staff on EU citizens

text_en: The Ministry of Infrastructure and Regional Development is amending sectoral legislation on access to service housing to remove gaps that would prevent Member State citizens' access to such housing.
summary: The Infrastructure Ministry is amending service-housing rules so Member State citizens are not prevented from accessing it.
extraction_note: Also Annex A normative action 3 (March 2026).
intervention_as_stated: Amendment of sectoral legislation on service housing

text_en: The Equality Council, as the national authority for promoting, monitoring and supporting equal treatment of all EU workers and their family members, will have to revise its rules of operation, organisational chart and staffing to carry out the new tasks under Law No. 200/2025, notably examining discrimination cases against Member State citizens and acting as national contact point.
summary: The Equality Council must revise its rules, structure and staffing to perform its new Law 200/2025 tasks on EU workers' equal treatment.
intervention_as_stated: Revision of the Equality Council's regulation, organigram and staffing

text_en: The Ministry of Internal Affairs will also determine how Member State citizens arriving in Moldova will be registered, which will serve as the basis for access to public services in Moldova. For this, MAI's secondary legislation needs revising.
summary: The Interior Ministry will set how arriving Member State citizens are registered as the basis for access to public services.
intervention_as_stated: Registration procedure for Member State citizens; revision of MAI secondary legislation

text_en: The General Inspectorate for Migration will take the necessary measures, especially technical ones, to inform Member State citizens in Moldova adequately about their rights and obligations and refer them to competent institutions for their integration.
summary: The Migration Inspectorate will take mainly technical measures to inform Member State citizens of their rights and refer them to competent institutions.
intervention_as_stated: IGM information and referral measures for Member State citizens

text_en: To ensure access of EU citizens and their family members to early education, primary, lower and upper secondary education, vocational and technical education and initial and continuing vocational training in the national education system, the Ministry of Education and Research is adjusting secondary legislation.
summary: The Education Ministry is adjusting secondary legislation to give EU citizens and family members access to all levels of national education and training.
intervention_as_stated: Adjustment of education secondary legislation for EU citizens and family members

text_en: Following the adoption of Law 200/2025, the Equality Council, given the new role of national authority for equal treatment of all EU and EEA workers and their families, will change its structure with an increased staff ceiling and strengthen the capacity of staff examining complaints of discrimination against EU citizens.
summary: The Equality Council will restructure, raise its staff ceiling and train staff handling discrimination complaints by EU citizens.
extraction_note: Section numbered 2.2 as printed, although it sits in subchapter 2.1.
intervention_as_stated: Restructuring and staff increase of the Equality Council

text_en: The Ministry of Education and Research will create opportunities to learn Romanian for EU and EEA citizens, including family members, who enter the education system, through the National Programme for learning Romanian by national minorities, including adults.
summary: The Education Ministry will offer Romanian language learning to EU and EEA citizens and family members entering the education system.
extraction_note: Linked to the education of migrant workers' children (Directive 77/486/EEC). The text adds that a new edition of the Programme for 2026-2028 will be drafted in 2025, with language centres and a teacher remuneration mechanism (pages 432-433); not extracted separately.
intervention_as_stated: Romanian language learning for EU and EEA citizens (Programul național privind învățarea limbii române)

text_en: For children who are family members of EU citizens enrolled in the national education system, Romanian language courses will be offered in the schools where they are enrolled.
summary: Children of EU citizens in national schools will be offered Romanian language courses in their schools.
intervention_as_stated: Romanian language courses for children of EU citizens

text_en: Preparatory work for full accession to the European Network of Employment Services (EURES) needs to continue.
summary: Preparatory work for full membership of EURES needs to continue.

text_en: The Republic of Moldova has drawn up an internal action plan for joining the EURES network and has assigned the National Employment Agency the role of National Coordination Office.
summary: Moldova has an internal action plan for joining EURES and has designated ANOFM as EURES National Coordination Office.
extraction_note: Two linked measures in one sentence (plan and designation, M2), kept as one item.
intervention_as_stated: Internal action plan for EURES accession; ANOFM as National Coordination Office

text_en: Government Decision No. 617/2024 amended Government Decision No. 990/2018 on the organisation and functioning of the National Employment Agency, ensuring partial alignment with Regulation (EU) 2016/589 on EURES.
summary: Government Decision 617/2024 amended ANOFM's statute, partially aligning with the EURES Regulation 2016/589.
intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 617/2024

text_en: Government Decision No. 607/2025 approving the Regulation on organising national activities within the European network of employment services ensured the partial transposition of a series of acts, as follows:
summary: Government Decision 607/2025 on national EURES activities ensured partial transposition of a series of EU acts.
extraction_note: The acts listed (pages 433-434) are Regulation (EU) 2016/589 and Implementing Decisions (EU) 2017/1256, 2017/1257 and 2018/1021; the lead-in carries the claim of partial transposition.
intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 607/2025

text_en: To complete accession to the EURES network, Moldova must continue implementing reforms, improve data exchange between the National Employment Agency and the European platform, and complete legislative alignment so that citizens can fully benefit from the network.
summary: To complete EURES accession Moldova must continue reforms, improve ANOFM–EURES platform data exchange and finish legislative alignment.
extraction_note: The converted text has an unclosed bracket "(în și" where an abbreviation seems to be missing. Theme: data exchange with an EU electronic platform.

text_en: Within ANOFM, staff of the Labour Migration and EURES Directorate and of the ICT Directorate are involved in the technical connection to EURES and the data exchange between EURES and ANOFM's "Labour Market" information system.
summary: ANOFM's EURES and ICT directorates handle the technical connection to EURES and data exchange with its Labour Market information system.
extraction_note: Closing quotation mark converted as "=".

text_en: Moldova has designated an observer member and an alternate member in the ESCO Working Group, which represents full alignment with Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/1020 on the European list of skills, competences and occupations needed for automated matching through the EURES common IT platform.
summary: Moldova designated an observer and alternate to the ESCO Working Group, stated as full alignment with Implementing Decision 2018/1020.
intervention_as_stated: Designation of members to the ESCO Working Group

text_en: With ANOFM assigned the role of EURES National Coordination Office, the responsible directorates are to carry out the technical measures for access to the EURES platform under the Commission Decisions. This will allow data exchange between ANOFM's "Labour Market" information system and EURES on vacancies and jobseekers' CVs.
summary: ANOFM is to take technical measures for EURES platform access, enabling vacancy and CV data exchange with its Labour Market system.
intervention_as_stated: Technical measures for access to the EURES platform

text_en: To implement the EURES acts effectively, ANOFM's capacity will need to be strengthened by ensuring interoperability of its information system with the EURES platform and by training ANOFM staff for effective work within EURES.
summary: ANOFM capacity is to be built through interoperability of its information system with the EURES platform and staff training.
extraction_note: Also Annex B actions 5 and 6.
intervention_as_stated: Interoperability of the ANOFM information system with EURES; staff training

text_en: On 2 May 2025, the Cooperation Agreement on Moldova's participation in the European Labour Authority (ELA) was signed in Bratislava.
summary: On 2 May 2025 Moldova signed in Bratislava the cooperation agreement on participation in the European Labour Authority.
extraction_note: Signature recorded as adopted. Also stated, without date, in the introduction (page 425) as part of the summary of the Commission report (M3).
intervention_as_stated: Acordul de cooperare privind participarea Republicii Moldova la Autoritatea Europeană a Muncii

text_en: After signing the agreement, Moldovan authorities started a dialogue with ELA to deepen cooperation in priority areas, including the Electronic Exchange of Social Security Information (EESSI) system.
summary: After signature, Moldovan authorities opened a dialogue with ELA on deeper cooperation, including on EESSI.
intervention_as_stated: Dialogue with ELA, including on EESSI

text_en: Work is under way on a draft law amending certain acts to harmonise national legislation with Regulation (EU) 2019/1149 and facilitate effective cooperation of Moldovan authorities with the European Labour Authority.
summary: A draft law aligning with the ELA Regulation 2019/1149 and facilitating cooperation with ELA is being prepared.
extraction_note: Also Annex A normative action 10.
intervention_as_stated: Draft law harmonising with Regulation (EU) 2019/1149

text_en: We are working on strengthening the capacities of MMPS, ANOFM and ISM, which will be the key authorities cooperating with the Authority.
summary: Capacity of the Labour Ministry, ANOFM and the Labour Inspectorate, the key ELA counterparts, is being strengthened.
intervention_as_stated: Capacity building of MMPS, ANOFM and ISM for cooperation with ELA

text_en: Coordination of social security systems: advancing negotiations with other EU Member States with a view to signing social security agreements.
summary: Objective: advance negotiations with further EU Member States to sign social security agreements.
extraction_note: Stated objective opening the subchapter (M1).
intervention_as_stated: Negotiation of social security agreements with EU Member States

text_en: social insurance [rights] of workers from the Republic of Moldova who work or have worked in another state, through 18 bilateral social security agreements concluded with other states (16 of them EU Member States).
summary: Moldova protects its workers' social insurance rights abroad through 18 bilateral social security agreements, 16 with EU Member States.
extraction_note: Quote starts mid-sentence at the top of page 437 (the sentence begins on page 436: "Republica Moldova asigură protejarea și garantarea drepturile de"), because the quote check drops one-word lines at page boundaries in this file. Contradicts page 437 (20 international social security agreements, 17 with EU Member States, plus 4 territoriality agreements); both recorded as stated for a contradicts link in pass 2. In scope under the G3 precedent on bilateral social security agreements.

text_en: Having obtained candidate status, Moldova commits to intensifying efforts to conclude social security agreements with all EU Member States and non-EU countries, in line with Regulation (EC) No 883/2004.
summary: As a candidate, Moldova commits to step up efforts to conclude social security agreements with all EU Member States and other countries.
intervention_as_stated: Social security agreements with all EU Member States

text_en: European Health Insurance Card: the Republic of Moldova is to apply the European Health Insurance Card (EHIC).
summary: Moldova is to apply the European Health Insurance Card.
intervention_as_stated: Application of the European Health Insurance Card (CEAS)

text_en: The Republic of Moldova has concluded 20 international social security agreements, 17 of them with EU Member States, based on the proportionality principle, allowing aggregation of insurance periods in both countries to establish benefit rights.
summary: Moldova has concluded 20 international social security agreements, 17 with EU Member States, allowing aggregation of insurance periods.
extraction_note: The list that follows names 18 states (17 EU Member States and Switzerland). Contradicts page 436-437 (18 agreements, 16 with EU Member States).

text_en: Moldova has also concluded 4 agreements on guarantees of citizens' pension rights, based on the territoriality principle, with Ukraine, Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.
summary: Moldova also has 4 territoriality-based pension agreements with Ukraine, Russia, Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

text_en: The social security agreements concluded by Moldova are based on the European principles set out in Regulation (EC) No 883/2004 on the coordination of social security systems,
summary: Moldova's social security agreements are based on the European principles of Regulation 883/2004.
extraction_note: Quote ends at the page break; the sentence continues on page 438 (principles accepted and applied by all EU Member States and non-EU states). The principles listed on page 438 are equal treatment, determination of applicable legislation, aggregation of insurance periods and export of benefits.

text_en: These agreements allow better social protection for Moldovan citizens working abroad and facilitate their access to social rights equivalent to those of EU citizens.
summary: The agreements give Moldovans working abroad better social protection and access to social rights equivalent to EU citizens'.
extraction_note: Concerns nationals abroad; kept because it is about the bilateral social security agreements (G3 precedent).

text_en: Currently the EU acts regulating the European Health Insurance Card are not transposed in Moldova.
summary: The EU acts on the European Health Insurance Card are not yet transposed in Moldova.

text_en: One of the main actions is amending national legislation, including Law No. 411/1995 on health care and Law No. 1585/1998 on compulsory health insurance. These amendments are planned during the year 2025/2026.
summary: To implement the EHIC, Laws 411/1995 and 1585/1998 on health care and health insurance are to be amended.
extraction_note: The year is converted as "202 5 6" (apparently 2025 corrected to 2026). Restated at page 440 with 2026, extracted there because the wording differs.
intervention_as_stated: Amendment of Laws 411/1995 and 1585/1998 for the EHIC

text_en: The institution (CNAS) implements the international social security treaties to which Moldova is party and is responsible for negotiating and signing international treaties under Law No. 595/1999.
summary: CNAS implements Moldova's social security treaties and negotiates and signs them.

text_en: The Directorate's planned staff is 5 specialists, of which 4 posts are currently filled.
summary: The Directorate (the Labour Ministry's social insurance policy directorate) has 5 planned posts, 4 filled.
extraction_note: The Directorate is the MMPS Direcția politici de asigurări sociale, whose aim includes coordinating social security systems with destination states of Moldovan migrant workers (preceding sentence).

text_en: General Directorate for International Relations (planned staff 18 specialists; 16 employed and involved);
summary: CNAS's international relations directorate has 18 planned posts and 16 staff involved.
extraction_note: Other CNAS subdivisions involved (legal, IT, external pensions, accounting) listed on page 439 are not extracted.

text_en: CNAM is the coordinator of the process of implementing the European Health Insurance Card.
summary: The National Health Insurance Company (CNAM) coordinates implementation of the European Health Insurance Card.
extraction_note: Designation of a role (M2).
intervention_as_stated: CNAM as EHIC implementation coordinator

text_en: IT Directorate: planned staff 8 specialists, of whom 3 are employed and involved in coordinating and monitoring development of the IT components for the EHIC and interconnection with European systems.
summary: Three of eight planned CNAM IT staff work on EHIC IT components and interconnection with European systems.

text_en: Moldova commits to signing social security agreements with all EU Member States by accession, in line with Regulation 883/2004, Regulation (EU) 2019/1149 and Regulation (EU) 1231/2010 (11 EU states).
summary: Moldova commits to sign social security agreements with all EU Member States, 11 remaining, before accession.
extraction_note: Differs from page 437 by the accession deadline and the figure of 11 states, so extracted again (M3).
intervention_as_stated: Social security agreements with all EU Member States by accession

text_en: In addition, we plan to adapt the legal framework to transpose Regulation (EC) No 987/2009 and ensure cross-border data exchange by accession.
summary: The legal framework is to be adapted for Regulation 987/2009 and cross-border social security data exchange by accession.
intervention_as_stated: Legal framework for Regulation 987/2009 and cross-border data exchange

text_en: There is also a commitment to implement the European Health Insurance Card, which requires amending Law No. 411/1995 on health care and Law No. 1585/1998 on compulsory health insurance. These amendments are planned for 2026.
summary: Moldova commits to implement the EHIC, amending Laws 411/1995 and 1585/1998 in 2026.
intervention_as_stated: EHIC implementation; amendment of Laws 411/1995 and 1585/1998

text_en: In Moldova, data exchange, including cross-border exchange, takes place exclusively through the interoperability platform (MConnect), managed by the e-Governance Agency, under Law No. 142/2018 and Government Decision No. 211/2019.
summary: All data exchange in Moldova, including cross-border, runs exclusively through the MConnect interoperability platform managed by the e-Governance Agency.
extraction_note: Stated in the EESSI context.
intervention_as_stated: Platforma de interoperabilitate MConnect

text_en: MDED, the e-Governance Agency, STISC, the Cyber Security Agency, CNAS, MMPS, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Health, CNAM, the State Tax Service and ANOFM are preparing the digital infrastructure needed to join EESSI.
summary: Eleven institutions are preparing the digital infrastructure needed to join EESSI.
extraction_note: Subjects list shortened to the main Chapter 2 bodies; ASC, MF, MS and SFS are also named.
intervention_as_stated: Digital infrastructure for EESSI accession
